content.text: A first 'draft' of a script is available at
https://github.com/jwestgard/fcrepo-serial-restore
. The approach is the following:
Read YAML configuration file to get the rest endpoint and backup locations, server credentials, and namespaces to filter;

Iterate over the serialized backup tree, reading each turtle file and (after filtering out server managed triples) PUTting the turtle to the resource location represented by the corresponding directory path.

Currently, my local fedora is returning a 403 response, I'm guessing because I haven't filtered out some triples that Fedora doesn't want me to be setting.  I'll keep working on it, but comments and advice welcomed!
ADDITIONAL FEATURES:
Add the uploading of binaries;
Support other serializations besides turtle;
Add configurable levels of logging to record the requests made and the server's responses;
Add support for resumability?  I don't know how difficult this will prove to be, but it seems like it could be important for large repositories.

Remember to be careful with direct and indirect containers. You may want to scan through the entire datastore in a first pass, looking for resources of those types, and then selectively removing the membership triples from the target resources.
You will also need to filter out ldp:contains triples (but clearly not everything in the LDP namespace)
Thanks,
. I knew there would be more to do to fine tune the relationships, but had hoped this first version could serve as a demonstration in the meantime.  I'll keep working on it.
, I am not sure if you are still working on this, but here are the results of running a simple test:
Start the karaf/camel/fcrepo-serialization service (by default it stores resources at '/tmp/descriptions')
Start an empty fcrepo
Run
for x in {0..100}; do echo $x; curl -XPUT localhost:8080/rest/container${x}; done
..followed by
for x in {0..100}; do echo $x; sed -e "s/XXXX/${x}/" dc-title.ru | curl -XPATCH -H"Content-Type: application/sparql-update" --upload-file - localhost:8080/rest/container${x}; done
..where "dc-title.ru" is:
This creates 100 containers with a dc:title property set.
Save then clear the contents of the stored '/tmp/descriptions/'
Start an empty fcrepo again (stop, clear the contents, and restart fcrepo)
In the fcrepo-serial-restore project, update the config.yml as appropriate
Run:
./restore.py -c config.yml
Compare the contents of the newly create contents of '/tmp/descriptions' with the original contents of that directory
The resources are named with the .ttl extension
The dc:title properties are gone
The original "fedora:created" and "fedora:lastModified" properties are not retained under some other property

Thanks, Andrew.  I have not been working on it actively because of other committments, but I do intend to resume work on it shortly.  Thanks for the feedback.  I think the frame of the script is a reasonable starting point, but clearly it is far too 'dumb' about the differences between the various LDP container types.  As
pointed out, I will need to iterate over the serialized resource tree and determine which containers are of which type, etc.

told me to interject despite probably sounding ignorant, but I was wondering if it was an assumption that this effort would be unaware (and therefore not support) version snapshots, or whether fcrepo-serialization already serialized snapshots separately.
fcrepo-serialization does not currently support version snapshots... therefore, this utility should not need to.
However, I would suggest the fcrepo-serialization add the option for snapshot support... and the round-tripping tooling should also follow.

This ticket is effectively dead given that the functionality that it seeks to implement has been completely superseded by fcrepo-import-export and the verification tooling.  Please close as you see fit.
This task is to create a standalone utility that can take the output of fcrepo-serialization [1] and load those resources (rdf and non-rdf) into an initially empty repository.
Special attention will need to be paid to the handling of server-managed triples and properties generated by Direct and Indirect container interaction models.
https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo-camel-toolbox/tree/master/fcrepo-serialization

  1. Read YAML configuration file to get the rest endpoint and backup locations, server credentials, and namespaces to filter;
  2. Iterate over the serialized backup tree, reading each turtle file and (after filtering out server managed triples) PUTting the turtle to the resource location represented by the corresponding directory path.

Currently, my local fedora is returning a 403 response, I'm guessing because I haven't filtered out some triples that Fedora doesn't want me to be setting. I'll keep working on it, but comments and advice welcomed!

ADDITIONAL FEATURES:

  1. Add the uploading of binaries;
  2. Support other serializations besides turtle;
  3. Add configurable levels of logging to record the requests made and the server's responses;
  4. Add support for resumability? I don't know how difficult this will prove to be, but it seems like it could be important for large repositories.

Remember to be careful with direct and indirect containers. You may want to scan through the entire datastore in a first pass, looking for resources of those types, and then selectively removing the membership triples from the target resources.

You will also need to filter out ldp:contains triples (but clearly not everything in the LDP namespace)
Thanks, Unknown. I knew there would be more to do to fine tune the relationships, but had hoped this first version could serve as a demonstration in the meantime. I'll keep working on it.

Joshua Allan Westgard, I am not sure if you are still working on this, but here are the results of running a simple test:

  1. Start the karaf/camel/fcrepo-serialization service (by default it stores resources at '/tmp/descriptions')
  2. Start an empty fcrepo
  3. Run 
    for x in {0..100}; do echo $x; curl -XPUT localhost:8080/rest/container${x}; done

    ..followed by

    for x in {0..100}; do echo $x; sed -e "s/XXXX/${x}/" dc-title.ru | curl -XPATCH -H"Content-Type: application/sparql-update" --upload-file - localhost:8080/rest/container${x}; done

    ..where "dc-title.ru" is:

    PREFIX dc: <http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/>

INSERT {
  <> dc:title "Some Title-XXXX"
} WHERE {}
    • This creates 100 containers with a dc:title property set.
  4. Save then clear the contents of the stored '/tmp/descriptions/'
  5. Start an empty fcrepo again (stop, clear the contents, and restart fcrepo)
  6. In the fcrepo-serial-restore project, update the config.yml as appropriate
  7. Run: 
    ./restore.py -c config.yml
  8. Compare the contents of the newly create contents of '/tmp/descriptions' with the original contents of that directory
    • The resources are named with the .ttl extension
    • The dc:title properties are gone
    • The original "fedora:created" and "fedora:lastModified" properties are not retained under some other property

Thanks, Andrew. I have not been working on it actively because of other committments, but I do intend to resume work on it shortly. Thanks for the feedback. I think the frame of the script is a reasonable starting point, but clearly it is far too 'dumb' about the differences between the various LDP container types. As Unknown pointed out, I will need to iterate over the serialized resource tree and determine which containers are of which type, etc.

A. Soroka told me to interject despite probably sounding ignorant, but I was wondering if it was an assumption that this effort would be unaware (and therefore not support) version snapshots, or whether fcrepo-serialization already serialized snapshots separately.

fcrepo-serialization does not currently support version snapshots... therefore, this utility should not need to.
However, I would suggest the fcrepo-serialization add the option for snapshot support... and the round-tripping tooling should also follow.
